item.title: Hombres enmascarados se manifiestan en puerto inglés de Dover, interrumpe tráfico a través del Canal de la Mancha
item.description: Las protestas de grupos de hombres enmascarados en las carreteras de los alrededores del puerto inglés de Dover, principal centro de conexión de los transbordadores que cruzan a Francia, interrumpieron el tráfico el sábado, según informaron la policía y las autoridades portuarias.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las protestas de grupos de hombres enmascarados en las carreteras de los alrededores del puerto inglés de Dover, principal centro de conexión de los transbordadores que cruzan a Francia, interrumpieron el tráfico el sábado, según informaron la policía y las autoridades portuarias. Los manifestantes, vestidos de negro y con pasamontañas, coreaban «Stop the boats» («Detengan los barcos»), según informó la BBC, en referencia a los solicitantes de asilo que llegan a la costa sur de Inglaterra desde Francia. Las principales carreteras de acceso al puerto quedaron bloqueadas el sábado por la mañana, pero el acceso al puerto se había restablecido y los participantes en la "protesta espontánea" se habían dispersado a mediodía, según informó la Policía de Kent en un comunicado el X. No se produjeron detenciones, según la policía. Los sucesivos gobiernos británicos han tenido dificultades para frenar el flujo de solicitantes de asilo, que a menudo llegan en embarcaciones neumáticas abarrotadas. Sin embargo, el número de llegadas este año hasta el 1 de septiembre ascendió a 16.513, lo que supone un descenso de alrededor del 43% respecto al mismo periodo de 2025, según datos del Gobierno citados por la BBC.

item.title: Enviados EEUU Witkoff y Kushner llegan a Moscú para mantener conversaciones sobre paz en Ucrania
item.description: Los representantes especiales de Estados Unidos, Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, aterrizaron el sábado en Moscú para mantener conversaciones sobre cómo poner fin a la guerra en Ucrania, donde fueron recibidos por el enviado presidencial ruso Kirill Dmitriev.
item.dc:creator: Gleb Bryanski
item.content:encoded: Los representantes especiales de Estados Unidos, Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, aterrizaron el sábado en Moscú para mantener conversaciones sobre cómo poner fin a la guerra en Ucrania, donde fueron recibidos por el enviado presidencial ruso Kirill Dmitriev. Una comitiva, en la que viajaban Witkoff, Kushner y Dmitriev, partió del aeropuerto gubernamental de Moscú y se dirigió hacia la ciudad, según informó un testigo de Reuters. El portavoz ruso, Dmitry Peskov, declaró a la agencia de noticias TASS que el presidente Vladimir Putin se reuniría con Witkoff y Kushner en el Kremlin más tarde ese mismo sábado. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, sugirió el viernes que Washington tenía una nueva propuesta concreta destinada a poner fin a la guerra, que ya cumple su quinto año. Sin embargo, no dio más detalles sobre en qué consistiría dicha propuesta. El enviado ruso Dmitriev, quien declaró a Reuters en junio que se había mantenido en contacto con los negociadores estadounidenses durante una pausa en sus visitas a Rusia, participó en todas sus reuniones anteriores con Putin junto al asesor de política exterior de este, Yuri Ushakov. También desempeñó un papel en la negociación de las exenciones a las sanciones estadounidenses sobre el petróleo ruso este año. El presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmó el viernes que ambos viajarían a Ucrania el domingo tras visitar Moscú. En una publicación en X el sábado, Zelenskiy señaló que Rusia había atacado dos aeropuertos ucranianos antes de la visita de los enviados estadounidenses a Kiev. Peskov afirmó en un comunicado publicado en el canal del Kremlin en la aplicación de mensajería Max que Putin había ordenado al ejército no atacar Kiev durante tres días, a partir de la medianoche del sábado, en relación con la visita de Witkoff y Kushner a la capital ucraniana. El Ministerio de Defensa ruso informó el sábado de la presencia de 53 drones ucranianos en el espacio aéreo ruso, una cifra significativamente inferior a la media registrada en los últimos meses. Moscú celebra este sábado el Día de la Ciudad, con cientos de miles de personas participando en las festividades al aire libre por toda la ciudad. Sigue existiendo una enorme brecha entre Rusia y Ucrania sobre cómo poner fin a la guerra, que ya dura cuatro años y medio y es la más mortífera en Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Una fuente cercana al Kremlin, que habló antes de que surgieran las noticias sobre un posible viaje de los enviados del presidente Trump, afirmó que Putin seguía decidido a conquistar más territorio. "No hay posibilidad de alcanzar un acuerdo sobre la línea del frente hasta que Putin termine de asegurar la parte restante de la región de Donetsk", declaró la fuente a Reuters, añadiendo que el líder del Kremlin confiaba —basándose en los informes de sus comandantes— en que esto ocurriría antes de que acabara el año.

item.title: Pursuing playoffs, Rangers turn to Jacob deGrom to try to shut down Rays
item.description: The Texas Rangers hope the "vintage" Jacob deGrom returns for his next start on Saturday evening against the Tampa Bay Rays.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers hope the "vintage" Jacob deGrom returns for his next start on Saturday evening against the Tampa Bay Rays. The 38-year-old deGrom (10-9, 4.00 ERA) is scheduled to start in the third game of a four-game series in Arlington, Texas, five days after the two-time National League Cy Young Award winner pitched one of the best games of his career. The Rangers and Rays have split the first two games of the series. deGrom allowed one hit and faced the minimum of 21 batters over seven innings in an 8-1 win against the visiting Athletics on Monday, becoming the first Rangers pitcher to face the minimum through seven innings since Jon Gray on June 7, 2023, against the St. Louis Cardinals. "That was vintage deGrom tonight," A's manager Mark Kotsay said. "He had his explosive fastball. The slider was anywhere from 94 (mph). I saw one against (Jeff) McNeil that just turned left. I thought he was probably at his best tonight." It marked the eighth time this season that the right-hander didn't issue a walk, and the third outing in which he surrendered just one hit. "It's special watching him cruise like that," Rangers first baseman Jake Burger said. "That's why he's one of the greats." The Rangers (70-72) sensed something special was brewing with deGrom after he surrendered eight runs in 3 2/3 innings in his previous start Aug. 25 against the Chicago White Sox, an outing that led to an 11-7 loss. "I'm pretty frustrated after most rough starts, but that one was really bad," deGrom said. "We can't afford to have those kinds of starts. That really bothered me. We needed to go out there and win games there, and I had an absolute terrible start. I needed to turn the page and prepare for this one. Hopefully, moving forward, I can continue to throw the ball how I expect to." Texas manager Skip Schumaker said he would like to see more consistency from deGrom, as well, as the Rangers chase a playoff berth. Texas stands three games out of first place in the American League West, behind the Houston Astros, and two games out of the AL's final wild-card spot. "There's been some really good starts, and then there's been some ones that he would tell you that have not been so great," Schumaker said. "After the last one, I felt like (against the A's) was going to be a really good day, just because he was so mad at what happened. "When you have a competitor like Jacob, who is pretty upset at the previous game or previous start, you knew that he was going to come in with a different type of mentality and be on the attack. And that's exactly what he did." The Rays (84-57) are one of the few MLB teams deGrom has not defeated in his career. He's 0-1 in four starts with a 3.00 ERA against them. Tampa Bay, which has the best record in the AL, plans to start right-hander Drew Rasmussen (14-5, 2.95 ERA) on Saturday. He went 5-0 in six starts in August while posting a 2.57 ERA. Rasmussen's most recent start last Sunday is the only one in which he did not earn a victory last month. He allowed two runs and four hits in six innings of a 5-4 win against the San Diego Padres in 11 innings, helping his team complete a sweep. "This is a series we can point to and tell our guys who haven't experienced postseason baseball, 'Every day is like this,'" Rasmussen said. "It's a roller-coaster ride. Games are close, and you win on the margins." Rasmussen has made three starts in his career against the Rangers, going 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA. He most recently faced them on June 3, 2025, and threw five shutout innings in a 5-1 victory. --Field Level Media

item.title: US military strikes three Iranian crude oil carriers, Central Command says

item.title: Ciudadano chino es rescatado de un túnel en Nepal diez días después de una crecida repentina
item.description: Las autoridades informaron que el sábado se rescató con vida a un ciudadano chino de un túnel en Nepal, diez días después de que una avalancha de hielo, rocas y barro arrasara un valle del Himalaya, causando la muerte de más de 1.300 personas.
item.dc:creator: Sahana Bajracharya, Navesh Chitrakar, Joseph Campbell
item.content:encoded: Las autoridades informaron que el sábado se rescató con vida a un ciudadano chino de un túnel en Nepal, diez días después de que una avalancha de hielo, rocas y barro arrasara un valle del Himalaya, causando la muerte de más de 1.300 personas. El ejército nepalí informó de que Lu Haitao fue rescatado del interior de un túnel de 225 metros en el proyecto hidroeléctrico Upper Trishuli-1. Se trata de la tercera persona rescatada con vida hasta la fecha de los distintos túneles en los que las autoridades creen que podrían quedar atrapadas 900 personas tras el desprendimiento de un glaciar ocurrido el 26 de agosto en la cuenca alta del río. El viernes, los equipos de rescate sacaron a dos personas de otro túnel de la central hidroeléctrica Upper Trishuli 3A, situada en el mismo río. Las autoridades indicaron que Lu no presentaba lesiones visibles y que sus signos vitales eran estables, aunque mostraba síntomas de hipotermia leve. Las imágenes difundidas por el ejército nepalí mostraban cómo recibía atención médica de urgencia dentro de un helicóptero, que lo trasladó a un hospital militar. Parecía agotado y desorientado, con barro seco y polvo en la piel y la ropa. Se vio a un médico uniformado con un estetoscopio examinándolo. Al menos 1.344 personas han perdido la vida en Nepal a causa de las inundaciones que arrasaron casas, calles y colegios en pueblos y aldeas cercanas a la frontera con el Tíbet chino, según informó el viernes la autoridad de gestión de catástrofes. Unas 4.887 personas siguen desaparecidas, entre ellas 583 ciudadanos extranjeros, muchos de ellos peregrinos y excursionistas. Hasta el viernes, China había informado de que el número de fallecidos en el Tíbet ascendía a 31, con otros 531 desaparecidos, incluidos ciudadanos extranjeros, según la agencia estatal de noticias Xinhua. Unos 261 ciudadanos extranjeros siguen desaparecidos en el Tíbet. El ejército nepalí informó de que el sábado también se rescató a una mujer, Chandika Kumari Shrestha, de su casa en Betrawati. En una imagen difundida por las autoridades, se la ve cubierta de barro en el interior de una estructura subterránea inundada, mientras los equipos de rescate le ofrecen agua y trabajan en un espacio reducido lleno de lodo espeso.

item.title: Russian Valieva's neutral athlete status revoked, source says
item.description: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva will not be able to compete internationally after the sport's ruling body revoked her neutral athlete status, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Tommy Lund
item.content:encoded: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva will not be able to compete internationally after the sport's ruling body revoked her neutral athlete status, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Saturday. Valieva, 20, was 15 when she became the centre of a global controversy at the 2022 Olympics, after a sample taken two months earlier tested positive for the banned substance trimetazidine. She has received a letter informing her of the International Skating Union's (ISU) decision to revoke her neutral status, the source said. The ISU declined to comment. Valieva's representatives were not immediately available for comment. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) [USN:L8N3JH1UU TEXT:"imposed"] a four-year ban on Valieva in 2024, with the penalty backdated to when she tested positive for trimetazidine, which prevents angina attacks, at the Russian national championships in December 2021. The failed test emerged after she had helped Russia win team gold at the Olympics, a result which was later [USN:R4N3ED00C TEXT:"annulled"], elevating the United States to the top of the podium. Valieva [USN:L8N3YX0EM TEXT:"returned "]to ice skating in February at the Russian Jumping Championships but remained ineligible for this year's Milano-Cortina Olympics. Russian athletes have been barred from competing under their national flags since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The ISU has established a pathway for select athletes to compete as individual neutral athletes subject to rigorous vetting. Russian athletes can compete as neutrals if they pass strict background checks. Without neutral status, skaters cannot enter ISU events, earn world ranking points or compete for global titles. The Ukrainian Figure Skating Federation (UFSF) last week urged the ISU to review its readmission of Russian and Belarusian competitors as individual neutral athletes, warning that its screening process failed to enforce basic neutrality rules. It called on the ISU to institute stricter background audits, implement continuous compliance monitoring, and require all applicants to publicly condemn Russia’s war in Ukraine.

FAST

Sept 5 : Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva will not be able to compete internationally after the sport's ruling body revoked her neutral athlete status, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Saturday. Valieva, 20, was 15 when she became the centre of a global controversy at the 2022 Olympics, after a sample taken two months earlier tested positive for the banned substance trimetazidine. She has received a letter informing her of the International Skating Union's (ISU) decision to revoke her neutral status, the source said. The ISU declined to comment. Valieva's representatives were not immediately available for comment.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) imposed a four-year ban on Valieva in 2024, with the penalty backdated to when she tested positive for trimetazidine, which prevents angina attacks, at the Russian national championships in December 2021. The failed test emerged after she had helped Russia win team gold at the Olympics, a result which was later annulled, elevating the United States to the top of the podium. Valieva returned to ice skating in February at the Russian Jumping Championships but remained ineligible for this year's Milano-Cortina Olympics.  Russian athletes have been barred from competing under their national flags since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The ISU has established a pathway for select athletes to compete as individual neutral athletes subject to rigorous vetting. Russian athletes can compete as neutrals if they pass strict background checks. Without neutral status, skaters cannot enter ISU events, earn world ranking points or compete for global titles. The Ukrainian Figure Skating Federation (UFSF) last week urged the ISU to review its readmission of Russian and Belarusian competitors as individual neutral athletes, warning that its screening process failed to enforce basic neutrality rules. It called on the ISU to institute stricter background audits, implement continuous compliance monitoring, and require all applicants to publicly condemn Russia’s war in Ukraine.

item.title: Konnor Griffin, Pirates chase series win against struggling Angels
item.description: It took 10 seconds for rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin to make an impact in his return to the Pittsburgh Pirates' lineup on Friday night after missing 49 games because of a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: It took 10 seconds for rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin to make an impact in his return to the Pittsburgh Pirates' lineup on Friday night after missing 49 games because of a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger. Make that 10.14 seconds, to be exact. That's how long it took Griffin to dash from first base to home in the second inning on a double down the right-field line by Jake Mangum and score the only run in a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels on Friday. "Two outs, as soon as he hit it I was thinking score, and (third base coach Tony) Beasley loves to send, and we did it. We got it done," Griffin said. "I'm not sure anybody else in the major leagues scores on that ball," Pittsburgh manager Don Kelly said. "That was unbelievable. ... That's Konnor. And the electricity that he brings overall, and what he's able to do and how he's able to change the game." It was the fifth win in the past six games for the Pirates (70-72), who remain 4 1/2 games behind the San Diego Padres in the race for the final National League wild-card playoff spot with 20 games to go. Pittsburgh will try to win its fourth consecutive series on Saturday night when it sends right-hander Braxton Ashcraft (14-5, 3.59 ERA) to the mound against Los Angeles left-hander Yusei Kikuchi (0-5, 5.65). It will be Ashcraft's first career appearance against the Angels. He is 5-1 with a 2.66 ERA over his last seven starts, including a 5-4 victory at St. Louis on Sunday, when he allowed two runs on six hits in five innings with three strikeouts. Los Angeles (53-88) has lost three straight games and 10 of its last 11. The Angels need to go at least 10-11 in their final 21 games to avoid the first 100-game loss season in franchise history. Kikuchi, an All-Star in 2025, is 1-1 with a 5.00 ERA in four career appearances (three starts) against Pittsburgh, including 1-0 with a 3.55 ERA in three appearances (two starts) at PNC Park. It will be Kikuchi's third start since he missed almost four months due to left shoulder inflammation. He took the loss in a 5-2 setback to the Philadelphia Phillies on Sunday in Anaheim, Calif., when he allowed two runs on six hits, a walk and three strikeouts in seven innings. It marked the first time since Aug. 20, 2025, against the Reds that he pitched seven innings. "I think my fastball was really good today, especially the fastball command," Kikuchi said after Sunday's game. "Being able to pitch inside, east-west, where I wanted to. I had no complaints." Both runs allowed came on solo homers, the first one in the third inning by J.T. Realmuto on a slider in the middle of the plate, and the second on a high splitter to Edmundo Sosa in the seventh. "I thought Kikuchi pitched great," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said. "I felt the location of his fastball was better. Used some breaking balls. Seven innings, two runs, and it was two solo shots, so I thought he pitched great." --Field Level Media

item.title: Perú decreta que militares y policías asuman control de penales de alta peligrosidad
item.description: Perú declaró estado de emergencia en cinco penales de alta peligrosidad para permitir que policías y militares tomen el control de esos recintos, en busca de frenar la inseguridad ciudadana, según un decreto del gobierno publicado el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Perú declaró estado de emergencia en cinco penales de alta peligrosidad para permitir que policías y militares tomen el control de esos recintos, en busca de frenar la inseguridad ciudadana, según un decreto del gobierno publicado el sábado. La emergencia, que tendrá una vigencia de 60 días, permitirá además a las fuerzas armadas y la policía ejecutar acciones para "garantizar el espacio aéreo y el espectro electromagnético inmediato de las cárceles", según el decreto del gobierno de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, quien asumió al poder a fines de julio. En un comunicado presidencial, el gobierno dijo que la medida busca combatir "a las organizaciones criminales que dirigen sus delitos desde las cárceles hacia el exterior". Los cinco penales en emergencia albergan cerca del 50% de los internos vinculados a organizaciones criminales, agregó. Perú enfrenta una ola de delincuencia con una tasa de homicidios que aumentó a 10,7 por cada 100.000 habitantes el año pasado, frente al 10,1 en el 2024, según datos oficiales. El domingo previo, un grupo de sicarios vestidos como policías asesinó a cuatro personas y secuestró a un empresario que operada una mina informal en el norte del país, y luego de unas horas fue liberado tras pagar un rescate, según la policía. El gobierno ha solicitado al Congreso poderes legislativos por 120 días para aprobar una serie de medidas contra el avance del crimen, entre ellas declarar a las organizaciones criminales como "terroristas"; además para prevenir los efectos del fenómeno climático de El Niño. La oposición en el Congreso ha mostrado reparos en el pedido de la líder derechista, que prometió en su campaña electoral mano dura contra la inseguridad como gobernó su padre, el fallecido exmandatario Alberto Fujimori, quien estuvo en prisión condenado por abusos a los derechos humanos.

item.title: Infantino asistirá al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice
item.description: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, asistirá el sábado al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice, el primer torneo organizado por el organismo rector del fútbol mundial desde que abandonara su propuesta de vender una participación en el Mundial.
item.dc:creator: Iain Axon
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, asistirá el sábado al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice, el primer torneo organizado por el organismo rector del fútbol mundial desde que abandonara su propuesta de vender una participación en el Mundial. El dirigente suizo descartó el plan —que valoraba los derechos comerciales de la Copa del Mundo y otros torneos de la FIFA en 20 000 millones de dólares— a finales de julio, ante la feroz reacción de los organismos regionales de gobierno, entre ellos la UEFA europea, y de las principales partes interesadas del deporte. Un portavoz de la Federación Polaca de Fútbol confirmó que Infantino, en medio de la polémica, estaría presente en el partido inaugural. Se espera que unas 15.000 personas asistan a los dos primeros partidos del sábado. El evento constituye un importante torneo de desarrollo para el fútbol femenino, ya que muchas de las jugadoras aspiran a participar en la Copa del Mundo femenina absoluta que se celebrará en Brasil el año que viene. Polonia se enfrentará a Argentina y México jugará contra Benín en Katowice en la jornada inaugural.

item.title: Embajador EEUU visita localidad palestina en medio de recrudecimiento de violencia de colonos en Cisjordania
item.description: El embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, Mike Huckabee , se reunió el sábado con palestinos estadounidenses, entre ellos familiares de ciudadanos estadounidenses asesinados por colonos israelíes, en una localidad palestina de la Cisjordania ocupada que ha sido objeto de ataques por parte de los colonos .
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: El embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, Mike Huckabee , se reunió el sábado con palestinos estadounidenses, entre ellos familiares de ciudadanos estadounidenses asesinados por colonos israelíes, en una localidad palestina de la Cisjordania ocupada que ha sido objeto de ataques por parte de los colonos . La visita se produce en un momento en que la violencia de los colonos —y lo que se percibe ampliamente como la inacción del Gobierno israelí— ha suscitado cada vez más condenas internacionales, incluso por parte de aliados de Estados Unidos. El Gobierno israelí ha condenado la violencia de los colonos, aunque los autores rara vez son detenidos y aún menos a menudo procesados. Washington no ha criticado al Gobierno del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu por la violencia, aunque ha pedido que se juzgue a los autores, a quienes Huckabee ha calificado de terroristas. Huckabee calificó de constructiva su reunión en Turmus Ayya, donde la mayoría de los residentes palestinos de la localidad son ciudadanos estadounidenses. Aunque Huckabee, pastor bautista y defensor desde hace mucho tiempo de los asentamientos israelíes, ha pedido anteriormente que se juzgue a los colonos violentos, también afirma que cree que estos representan una minoría de la comunidad de colonos, que asciende a unos 750.000. Alrededor de tres millones de palestinos viven en Cisjordania, y se estima que decenas de miles de ellos son ciudadanos estadounidenses. Los palestinos de Cisjordania se han enfrentado a un recrudecimiento de la violencia de los colonos, al tiempo que sus libertades se han visto cada vez más restringidas bajo la ocupación militar desde que la coalición de Netanyahu, la más de extrema derecha de la historia de Israel, llegó al poder a finales de 2022. En Turmus Ayya, los palestinos se enfrentan a lo que el alcalde Nawwaf Zaghoul ha calificado de ataques constantes por parte de los colonos. Según él, alrededor del 80 % de los residentes de esta localidad palestina tienen la ciudadanía estadounidense. Alrededor de la localidad se han establecido asentamientos israelíes, entre ellos Shiloh, que Huckabee ha visitado en dos ocasiones desde 2025. Huckabee, el primer cristiano evangélico en ocupar el cargo de embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, se refiere a Cisjordania como Judea y Samaria, su nombre bíblico, que utiliza el Gobierno israelí pero que no ha sido adoptado por Estados Unidos. Huckabee declaró a los periodistas en Turmus Ayya que al Gobierno israelí le interesaba tomar medidas contra quienes llevaban a cabo "conductas delictivas y actos de terrorismo", y que un "pequeño grupo de meros merodeadores", que según él ascendía a unos pocos cientos de personas, estaba dañando la reputación del país.

item.title: Croatie Manifestation à Zagreb pour réclamer le nettoyage de déchets
item.description: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes se sont rassemblées samedi sur la place centrale de Zagreb pour protester contre l'inaction du gouvernement face à l'accumulation de plus de 30.000 tonnes de déchets dans une région du centre de la Croatie.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes se sont rassemblées samedi sur la place centrale de Zagreb pour protester contre l'inaction du gouvernement face à l'accumulation de plus de 30.000 tonnes de déchets dans une région du centre de la Croatie. La manifestation, l'une des plus importantes en Croatie depuis plusieurs années, a été baptisée "Marche pour la Lika", du nom de la région montagneuse où sont stockés les déchets. Les autorités ont découvert l'an dernier entre 34.000 et 37.000 tonnes de déchets, importés d'Italie pour la plupart entre 2023 et 2024, sur un site proche de la ville de Gospic, dans la région de Lika en Croatie. Le gouvernement s'est engagé à dépolluer le site, mais les organisations environnementales dénoncent le peu de progrès réalisés. Les écologistes affirment que ces détritus, où figurent des déchets médicaux et industriels, contaminent l'air, le sol et l'eau de Lika, une région réputée pour ses vastes étendues naturelles préservées. Ils reprochent au gouvernement sa lenteur à les éliminer. Les manifestants brandissaient des banderoles sur lesquelles on pouvait lire : "Les poumons de la Croatie ne peuvent plus respirer", "Arrêtez la destruction de la Croatie" et "La nature ne pardonne pas". "Nous sommes insatisfaits de la réponse du gouvernement. Le site aurait dû être nettoyé depuis longtemps", a déclaré Verica Jurnjak, venue de Gospić pour l'occasion. "C’est une honte que personne ne se soucie de nos enfants et de leur avenir." Le Premier ministre, Andrej Plenkovic, s'est rendu à Gospic mercredi et a déclaré que le gouvernement avait désigné un entrepreneur pour la première phase de nettoyage consistant à retirer les déchets du site. L'acteur croate Rade Serbedzija, internationalement connu pour ses rôles dans des films hollywoodiens tels que "Snatch" et "Mission : Impossible II", était présent à la manifestation. "Je suis ici parce que je dois y être. C’est notre devoir de défendre notre pays", a-t-il déclaré. "Ce qui s’est passé est une honte, et quelqu’un doit en répondre."

item.title: Racism has no place in Singapore; concerns about SIA-Air India deal ‘purely commercial’, says WP MP Kenneth Tiong
item.description: The Workers' Party MP was responding to comments by Senior Minister K Shanmugam on Saturday (Sep 5), in which he addressed racist online comments about the Nepal-Tibet disaster and SIA’s investment in Air India.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Racism has no place in Singapore; concerns about SIA-Air India deal ‘purely commercial’, says WP MP Kenneth Tiong

The Workers' Party MP was responding to comments by Senior Minister K Shanmugam on Saturday (Sep 5), in which he addressed racist online comments about the Nepal-Tibet disaster and SIA’s investment in Air India.

FAST

SINGAPORE: Workers' Party Member of Parliament Kenneth Tiong on Saturday (Sep 5) said there is "no place for racism in our society" as he defended his criticism of Singapore Airlines' (SIA) investment in Air India, saying his concerns were "purely commercial". Mr Tiong was responding to comments by Senior Minister K Shanmugam to reporters earlier on Saturday, when he condemned "shameful" racist and xenophobic online comments about the Nepal-Tibet disaster and SIA’s investment in Air India.  Mr Shanmugam, who is also home affairs minister and coordinating minister for national security, said decisions on whether to invest further in Air India rest with SIA, while Temasek, as a shareholder, expects the airline to make its investment decisions responsibly. He added that while Mr Tiong is entitled to his views on the deal, they should not substitute for the commercial judgement of SIA’s management and board of directors.

Mr Tiong raised concerns about SIA’s investment in Air India after Reuters reported last month that Air India had sought a further US$1.5 billion in support from owners Tata Sons and SIA, just months after it had posted a record annual loss. On Saturday, Mr Tiong said in a Facebook post he agreed with Mr Shanmugam that racism has no place in Singapore, and that he condemned any attacks on someone’s motives because of their ethnicity.  He said the debate over SIA's investment in Air India had become entangled with racist comments, which he condemned without reservation. “My concerns were, and are, purely commercial,” he said. In his Facebook post, Mr Tiong again raised concerns about SIA’s stake in Air India, questioning how many more times Air India might be asking shareholders for additional funding, and who would foot the bill when SIA is unable to.

Related:

Temasek backs SIA's Air India investment amid growing scrutiny

Police looking into 'shameful' racist online comments about Nepal-Tibet disaster, Air India: SM Shanmugam

Earlier on Saturday, Mr Shanmugam said reports that Air India was seeking fresh equity had triggered a new wave of "anti-Indian, racist ranting" online. He also said Temasek chief executive Dilhan Pillay Sandrasegara had been targeted because of his ethnicity. Regarding SIA’s investment in Air India, he said it is SIA's responsibility to assess its investments in Air India against the resources it has for its "long-term growth and profitability". "Any decision to invest in Air India lies with SIA, and Temasek as a shareholder in SIA, along with other shareholders, will expect SIA to make its investment decisions responsibly." While Temasek is accountable to the government for its overall portfolio and long-term performance, it is not accountable for individual investment decisions of its portfolio companies, Mr Shanmugam said. "Temasek and its subsidiaries decide how to invest across a wide portfolio with investments of varied risks and varied time horizons. Once governments or politicians start directing individual investment decisions, commercial discipline will be compromised," he added. "Decisions will become politicised – shaped by political considerations, rather than commercial judgment. In the end, Singaporeans will bear the cost." On Mr Tiong’s previous comments about SIA’s investment in Air India, Mr Shanmugam said: “Mr Tiong is entitled to his views. He is entitled, like any other Singaporean, to ask questions about SIA and Temasek.” "But neither his views, nor that of any minister, or any other MP, should substitute for the commercial judgment of SIA's management and board of directors – boards which have knowledgeable and independent members, and management which has professionals whose primary responsibility is to consider and make these decisions." Asked by a reporter whether Mr Tiong's post had crossed racial or xenophobic lines, he said: "As regards to Mr Tiong and whether he was being xenophobic or racist, I think you'd best ask him. You'd have to ask him what he intended and what he meant." On Mr Tiong's previous statement that no one "owes Air India a living", Mr Shanmugam said: "I think he ought to do his homework and look at SIA's letter and the facts that I put out today, and ask if he is being responsible." In his Facebook post on Saturday, Mr Tiong said that Singaporeans are best served when there is both zero tolerance for racism and hard questions about money.  “We should not let the two get mixed up. If we do, both causes suffer.”

Source: CNA/co(bg)

item.title: Juan Soto, Mets strive to claim series against Rafael Devers and Giants
item.description: Juan Soto and Rafael Devers are putting up big numbers for sub-.500 teams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Juan Soto and Rafael Devers are putting up big numbers for sub-.500 teams. Soto and the New York Mets will look to clinch another series win on Saturday afternoon, when they host Devers and the San Francisco Giants in the middle game of a three-game set. Left-hander Zac Thornton (3-4, 2.93 ERA) will start for the Mets against Giants right-hander Anthony Molina (2-0, 3.77). The Mets hit five home runs on Friday, when Nolan McLean grinded through six innings and earned the win as New York held off a late Giants rally in a 10-6 victory. Soto didn't get in on the homer-hitting fun Friday, when he finished 0-for-4 with an RBI forceout, a run and a stolen base. Francisco Alvarez delivered a pair of solo blasts while Mark Vientos (three-run homer), Bo Bichette (two-run homer) and Francisco Lindor (two-run homer) went deep with at least one runner on. But Soto's presence in the lineup after missing five weeks with a strained left calf is a reminder the Mets (64-77) haven't given up on the season despite residing in last place in the National League East for much of the summer. Soto is 4-for-21 with two homers and four RBIs in six games since his return. But his season-long OPS of .934 would rank second in the NL -- behind leading NL Most Valuable Player candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong -- if he had enough plate appearances to qualify and is just below his career mark of .947. "Anytime you are stepping on the field (in) a major league game, games are important and wins and losses are important," Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said Friday. "I think that's what Juan's presence means. That's what him battling to get back as quickly as he (did) means to us and to the group." Staying healthy hasn't been a problem this season for Devers, who has played in all 142 games while serving as one of the few bright spots for the Giants (58-84), who are on pace for just their second 90-loss season since 2009. Devers single-handedly kept the Giants in the game Friday, when he finished 3-for-4 with five RBIs. He opened the scoring for San Francisco with a two-run double in the third inning and hit a three-run homer in the eighth to pull the visitors to 9-6 and force the Mets to go to closer Kodai Senga. Alvarez hit his second homer in the bottom of the eighth, after which Senga threw a hitless ninth in a non-save situation. Devers has at least two hits in seven of his last 12 games, a stretch in which he is hitting .413 with seven homers and 18 RBIs. He has 33 homers, five shy of his career high set with the Boston Red Sox in 2021 and the most for a San Francisco slugger since all-time home run king Barry Bonds went deep 45 times in 2004. "Attitude, preparation, all those things are just spilling out on the field during the game," Giants manager Tony Vitello said. "You are seeing an exceptional player be who he is." Thornton didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he allowed two runs over five innings as the Mets fell to the Houston Astros 6-3. Molina earned the victory in his first start of the season on Monday after giving up three runs over five innings in the Giants' 7-3 win over the Atlanta Braves. Thornton has never opposed the Giants, and Molina is 0-0 with a 9.00 ERA in two career relief appearances against the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Farage and Bardella's 'small boats' pact draws criticism in France - Reuters
item.description: Farage and Bardella's 'small boats' pact draws criticism in France Reuters

item.title: Farage and Bardella's 'small boats' pact draws criticism in France
item.description: A plan agreed by Britain's populist Reform UK party and France's National Rally, aimed at sending asylum seekers who arrive in Britain in small boats back to France, drew criticism from several French presidential election candidates on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A [USN:L6N44W0QT TEXT:"plan"] agreed by Britain's populist Reform UK party and France's National Rally, aimed at sending asylum seekers who arrive in Britain in small boats back to France, drew criticism from several French presidential election candidates on Saturday. A memorandum of understanding signed on Friday by Reform leader Nigel Farage and National Rally (RN) chief Jordan Bardella is intended to go into effect if the two parties win power. Edouard Philippe, a former prime minister who is the conservative presidential candidate for the Horizons party in the 2027 election, said the pact was a "U-turn" for RN. "Seeing Jordan Bardella sign an agreement that provides for sending back to France migrants intercepted in the Channel, that one we didn't see coming," he said, asking whether the party's presidential candidate, Marine Le Pen, was "on the same page" as Bardella. Former Prime Minister and leader of the center-right Renaissance party Gabriel Attal said the pact showed the "submission " of the National Rally to foreign interests. "We are reaching levels of unpreparedness and submission that are almost never seen in the recent history of the National Rally. This shows their foreign policy is one of great submission to other powers," Attal said. Far-left leader and presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said on X that if the deal comes to fruition, "Our country would become the gatekeeper of the English. Not voting for Le Pen in 2027 becomes a matter of national dignity." Centre-left candidate Raphaël Glucksmann of the Place Publique party told BFM TV: "That's the hallmark of the National Rally: weakness when it comes to defending France's interests. Look at their votes in the European Parliament...We are the true patriots." Bardella dismissed the criticism. "So I welcome this agreement, and if tomorrow we are in power, and Nigel Farage is as well, we will do everything in our power to curb immigration both in France and in England," he said.

item.title: At their home away from home, Brewers pursue another win against Reds
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have made themselves at home at Great American Ball Park this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Milwaukee Brewers have made themselves at home at Great American Ball Park this season. The Brewers will look to record their fifth win in as many games in Cincinnati this season on Saturday when they play the second contest of their three-game series versus the Reds. Milwaukee is 7-1 on the season against the Reds. Milwaukee benefited from a costly error by shortstop Elly De La Cruz that helped ignite a five-run fifth inning in a 10-7 victory in the series opener on Friday. De La Cruz misplayed a possible double play, leading to bases loaded for the Brewers with no outs. Brice Turang was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded and rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch to send the Brewers (88-54) to the win against the Reds (67-74). Turang went 3-for-4 with three RBIs on Friday after going 3-for-24 with 11 strikeouts in his previous six games. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy was asked if the struggling second baseman is being adversely affected by his knee injury. "He's affected, but it all comes down (to) guys go through ups and downs every season," Murphy said. "Remember two weeks ago when we were panicked about (Christian) Yelich?" Yelich hit only .229 in August but perhaps has righted the ship since the calendar flipped to September, going 5-for-15 with one homer, two RBIs and five runs during his four-game hitting streak. Cincinnati manager Terry Francona doesn't seem as concerned about facing Yelich or Turang as he does his team's defense, namely what happened on De La Cruz's error. "I went back and looked at it a couple times," Francona said. "It went right in between (base runner William) Contreras' legs. I don't know if it snuck up on Elly after that. It was unfortunate." The loss spoiled a banner day for the Venezuela-born Eugenio Suarez, who belted a three-run homer in his return following a two-game absence due to taking the U.S. naturalization test in Miami. "It's very, very cool," Francona said of Suarez becoming a U.S. citizen. "He was excited and he should be. It's very neat." Suarez will look for a repeat performance against Milwaukee right-hander Dustin May (6-9, 4.69 ERA), who will look to record his first win in nearly one full month on Saturday. Acquired from the St. Louis Cardinals at the trade deadline, May won his first start with the Brewers on Aug. 6, 5-2 over the Pittsburgh Pirates. May fell to 0-2 in his past four starts after allowing four runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-4 setback to the Texas Rangers on Sunday. He pitched well in his lone career encounter versus Cincinnati on July 24 as a member of the Cardinals. He took a no-decision despite permitting one run on seven hits in six innings of the 4-2 loss. Reds left-hander Andrew Abbott (6-10, 4.49) will provide the opposition on Saturday. Abbott lost his third straight start last Saturday, tying season highs in runs (seven) and hits (eight) allowed in a 17-5 shellacking by the Chicago Cubs. He gave up three homers in his three innings of work. He received a no-decision in his lone appearance versus Milwaukee this season, allowing two runs on five hits -- albeit with five walks -- in five innings in a 4-2 loss. All told, Abbott is 3-4 with a 3.73 ERA in nine career appearances (all starts) against the Brewers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tens of thousands rally in Zagreb over Croatia waste cleanup delays - Reuters
item.description: Tens of thousands rally in Zagreb over Croatia waste cleanup delays Reuters

item.title: Tens of thousands rally in Zagreb over Croatia waste cleanup delays
item.description: Tens of thousands of people gathered in Zagreb's central square on Saturday to protest the government's failure to begin cleaning up more than 30,000 tons of waste in central Croatia that environmentalists say is polluting the drinking water in the area.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people gathered in Zagreb's central square on Saturday to protest the government's failure to begin cleaning up more than 30,000 tons of waste in central Croatia that environmentalists say is polluting the drinking water in the area. The protest, one of the biggest in Croatia in several years, was dubbed "Walk for Lika", after the mountainous region where the waste is stored. Authorities last year uncovered between 34,000 and 37,000 tons of waste, much of it imported from Italy in 2023 and 2024, at a site near the town of Gospic in Croatia's Lika region. The government pledged to clean up the site, but environmental groups say little progress has been made. Environmentalists say the waste, which they say includes medical and other industrial waste, is contaminating air, soil and water in Lika, a region known for its vast areas of unspoiled nature. They accuse the government of moving too slowly to remove it. Protesters carried banners reading: "The Lungs of Croatia Can No Longer Breathe", "Stop the Destruction of Croatia" and "Nature Does Not Forgive". "We are dissatisfied with the government's response. The site should have been cleaned up a long time ago," said Verica Jurnjak, who travelled from Gospić to attend the rally. "It is a shame that no one cares about our children and their future." Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic visited Gospic on Wednesday and said the government had selected a contractor for the first phase of the cleanup, which involves removing waste from the site. Croatian actor Rade Serbedzija, internationally known for his roles in Hollywood films including "Snatch" and "Mission: Impossible II", also attended the protest. "I am here because I have to be here. It is our duty to stand up for our country," he said. "What has happened is a disgrace, and someone must be held accountable."

item.title: Slugging White Sox hope to capitalize on comforts of home again vs. Twins
item.description: The Chicago White Sox often turn a pitcher's mistake into deep home runs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago White Sox often turn a pitcher's mistake into deep home runs. The White Sox (74-67) will try to keep their power surge going when they host the Minnesota Twins (67-74) on Saturday night. The White Sox are coming off a 4-1 win in Friday night's series opener, in which they hit three home runs. Colson Montgomery belted a two-run shot to right-center field, and Braden Montgomery and Miguel Vargas each ripped solo shots to the same part of the park. Twins manager Derek Shelton knows his pitchers have their hands full this weekend. "They're leading the American League in runs scored," Shelton said about the White Sox. "And in this ballpark (Rate Field), if you get the ball in the air, (it's trouble). ... They do a really good job of capitalizing on mistakes, and they've done it all year long." Colson Montgomery and Vargas each hit his 30th home run of the season on Friday. Chicago holds a 2 1/2-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians for first place in the American League Central with 21 games to go. The White Sox are looking to capitalize on their ability to win at home, where they are 42-27 this season. Only the Tampa Bay Rays (47-25) have more home wins in the AL. White Sox general manager Chris Getz praised manager Will Venable for the job he has done with a young team this season. Getz also praised Munetaka Murakami, who has 29 homers and 59 RBIs in his first year in the majors. Getz expressed a willingness to seek a contract extension with Murakami, a 26-year-old who starred in Japan before coming to play in the majors. "He's been a part of the success that we've had this year," Getz said Friday. "It's helped us win games. It's helped others gain confidence up here and believe that you can win games. That's certainly something that we're grateful for and thankful that we've gotten the opportunity to get to know him further. "He's a tremendous teammate, hard worker, and he's been productive." Twins right-hander Taj Bradley (10-6, 3.85 ERA) will try to silence Murakami and his fellow White Sox hitters on Saturday. Bradley leads Minnesota with 178 strikeouts in 154 1/3 innings and is the only pitcher on the staff with double-digit wins. In his most recent outing, he earned the victory on Monday after limiting the Detroit Tigers to one run on four hits in seven innings. He walked three and struck out nine in an 11-1 win. Bradley has faced the White Sox four times in his career, with turbulent results. He is 0-2 with a 10.47 ERA and has allowed 19 runs on 28 hits and 10 walks in 16 1/3 innings. Five walks came on June 3 in an 8-0 loss as Bradley allowed four runs on seven hits over 4 2/3 innings. He struck out five. Chicago will counter with left-hander Anthony Kay (9-7, 4.28 ERA). He is winless in his past four starts and is looking for his first victory since an Aug. 8 triumph over Cleveland. In one career start against Minnesota, Kay is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA. In a 3-1 home win on May 25, he held the Twins to one run on five hits and a walk in six innings. He struck out five. Shelton acknowledged that time is running out for the Twins to make a push for a wild-card playoff spot. With 21 games to go, the Twins stand 4 1/2 games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. "It's challenging," Shelton said after Friday's loss. "(If) this game happens in May, you're like, 'Hey, we got pitched to a little bit.' But as the calendar gets shorter, it's even more challenging." --Field Level Media

item.title: Tensions simmering ahead of Orioles' rematch with Red Sox
item.description: Late-season intensity has been on display in the first two games of Boston's series against the host Baltimore Orioles.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Late-season intensity has been on display in the first two games of Boston's series against the host Baltimore Orioles. That could be part of the backdrop as the Red Sox go for their third consecutive victory when the teams meet Saturday night. Boston won its second one-run game in a row with a 1-0 decision Friday night - and by the end there were signs of tempers flaring. Tensions were brewing after a confrontation between Baltimore's Blaze Alexander, who was a base runner, and Boston second baseman Nick Sogard. This came after Alexander slid into the base as the Red Sox pulled off an eighth-inning double play. "It's a competitive game," Sogard said. "He slid in pretty hard. I didn't have a problem with his slide, but we turned the double play. I was just looking back to see how far he went. I don't know if he liked me looking back. But that was pretty much it." Alexander said he didn't want to make a big deal of the incident. "I don't know why they're upset," Alexander said. "I didn't touch him. There was more contact on the play (Thursday) night. And that's it." The Red Sox (77-65) have won two games in a row as they try to show more signs of getting out of a rut. Yet they've won only four of their last 10 games. The Orioles (69-73) have dropped the first two games of the homestand to extend their overall losing streak to four games. "It's always disappointing to lose four in a row, especially right now at this point in the season where we're at," manager Craig Albernaz said. "Yeah, it's hard, and we've done it to ourselves. We're here, and there's a game tomorrow and we still have a chance, a good chance to kind of keep this thing going." It was a missed opportunity for Baltimore given that starting pitcher Shane Baz had a strong effort Friday. A first-inning pitch that resulted in Mickey Gasper's home run proved costly. Baz worked into the seventh inning. "He knew where the bullpen was at and he felt good enough to go back out there," Albernaz said of the importance of allowing the team's relievers to mostly regroup. "It was an outstanding outing from Shane. We couldn't get anything going off of (Boston starter Ranger) Suarez." Boston starter Sonny Gray (16-4, 2.82 ERA) will attempt to add to his win total, which is tied for the top mark in the majors with Philadelphia Phillies ace Cristopher Sanchez. Gray skipped a start since last working Aug. 26 in a loss at Miami when he gave up two runs in five innings. Gray hasn't faced the Orioles this year, but he's 7-6 with a 4.37 ERA in 15 all-time starts against Baltimore. The Orioles will turn to right-hander Chris Bassitt (6-4, 4.97 ERA) as their starting pitcher. He is in search of a victory in his third consecutive start after besting both the St. Louis Cardinals and the Athletics. Largely because of time off with an injury, Bassitt has pitched in only one home game since late May. His only June appearance resulted in a loss at Boston, where he allowed three runs in three innings. For his career, he's 2-4 with 3.88 ERA in 10 starts versus the Red Sox. --Field Level Media

item.title: Greek F-4 crashes during air show near Athens, two pilots dead, sources say
item.description: A Greek two-seat F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed on Saturday during an air show at Tanagra air base north of Athens, killing the pilots, two officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Greek two-seat F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed on Saturday during an air show at Tanagra air base north of Athens, killing the pilots, two officials told Reuters. "Unfortunately the two pilots are dead," one of the officials said, adding that the Phantom crashed about two kilometres outside the airport and there were no reports of injuries to any bystanders or residents in the wider area. Footage from public broadcaster ERT showed the F-4 performing a right turn a few meters above the ground seconds before it crashed and erupted into a fireball. Eleven firefighting aircraft and helicopters were operating to contain the fire that spread to the nearby forest. "We were all stunned. It hadn't been airborne for more than three minutes," an eyewitness told ERT. Loudspeakers at the air base were urging people to leave the area. The F-4 was participating in the Athens Flying Week, an annual event that attracts military and civilian aviation teams from dozens of countries.

FAST

PARIS, Sept 5 : Paris St Germain have not had as poor a start to a league season for 19 years, with Friday’s home loss to Monaco leaving them winless after three matches in the Ligue 1 season. Days before they begin the defence of their Champions League title, however, the Parisians have handed coach Luis Enrique a contract extension until 2030. “There is no reason to be concerned. I say that honestly. How many shots on target did Monaco have? Two. How many goals? Two. We’ll see at the end of the season whether things balance out,” he said after Friday’s 2-1 setback in which they were ahead at halftime but conceded twice after the break. “What I want to get across is that you shouldn’t look only at the result," Luis Enrique added. "We pressed sensationally, much better than in many matches when we did not concede a goal. But luck was not on our side.

“Monaco know that if they play against us like this 10 times, we win eight, there’d be one draw and we’d lose once. This was that one defeat,” Luis Enrique insisted as PSG look ahead to hosting Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday in their first Champions League group game, chasing a third successive European title. Two points from three matches is their worst start since the 2007-08 season, when PSG came close to relegation, finishing 16th. In that campaign, Paul Le Guen’s side had to wait until their sixth league game to record a victory and ended up only three points above the relegation places. This time round, the Parisians are already seven points off the pace. “It is incredible motivation for my players, for the team and for the club. If you want to bet on who will be champions at the end of the season, we can place a bet. Seven points? OK, we will try to make up that deficit as quickly as possible,” the coach added.

item.title: プーチン大統領、キーウへの攻撃停止を命じる－米特使の訪問に合わせ
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ロシアのプーチン大統領は、ウクライナの首都キーウへの空爆を3日間停止するようロシア軍に命じた。米国のウィトコフ、クシュナー両特使は協議のためモスクワに到着し、その後キーウを訪問する予定だ。

ロシア大統領府は、ウクライナ側も攻撃を3日間停止するとの情報を得ている。ペスコフ同大統領府報道官が確認した。5日にモスクワに到着したウィトコフ氏とクシュナー氏は、この後プーチン氏と会談する予定だと、ペスコフ氏は述べた。

ロシア大統領府に近い複数の関係者によると、今回の訪問で事態が進展するとの期待は極めて低い。両特使によるこれまでの訪ロでは進展がなく、今回ロシアにとって受け入れ可能な提案を両氏が持参していると考える理由もないという。

ペスコフ氏は5日、米国の提案について先走った見方をしないよう警告し、プーチン氏と両特使の会談を待つよう求めた。

関係者によれば、プーチン氏は自らの条件が満たされた場合にのみ戦争を終結させる用意がある。ロシア側はウクライナに対して軍事的に優位にあるとみており、要求を一段と強めているという。関係者は機微に触れる問題を話しているとして、匿名を条件に語った。

ウィトコフ、クシュナー両氏の訪問を巡って意味のある進展が得られるかについては、ウクライナ政府も悲観的だ。同国政府の考えを知る複数の関係者が明らかにした。両特使は、ウクライナ東部ドンバス地方に自由経済区を設けるといった従来案をあらためて働き掛けるとみられるが、ロシア側は既にこうした案を拒否しているという。

トランプ米大統領は4日、両特使が「戦争終結に向けた提案を携えている」と大統領執務室で述べたが、詳細には言及しなかった。

ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は4日遅く、ウィトコフ氏とクシュナー氏が6日にウクライナを訪れる予定だとXに投稿した。両氏のウクライナ訪問は戦争開始後で初めてとなる。

ゼレンスキー氏は、両氏の訪問を「可能な限り建設的かつ実質的なもの」にすることが、ウクライナ側の目標だと表明。また、両氏による訪問に必要な期間、ウクライナは空爆を実施しないと述べた。ロシア側も今回、これに応じる形で空爆停止を表明した。

item.title: Families of missing pilgrims in Tibet demand answers from China
item.description: Several families allege an information blackout in China.
item.dc:creator: Ju-min Park
item.content:encoded: Priyanka Choudhary, an Indian-born Finnish citizen returning from a Hindu pilgrimage in Tibet, was at a border crossing with Nepal when a catastrophic mudslide hit. She is one of 261 foreign nationals still missing in Tibet 10 days [USN:L1N44X01T TEXT:"after the disaster"], and her family and others seeking lost relatives are expressing frustration at Beijing's response. "There is no information on the China side," said Choudhary's brother Tarun. "We can't go to China and talk to anyone, so I'm not able to understand how things are... There is no update from China about what is happening at Ground Zero, what is the situation over there." The mudslide [USN:L4N44V129 TEXT:"that devastated"] the Tibet-Nepal border last week killed more than 1,300 people with more than 5,600 missing on both sides. In Tibet, at least 31 people have been confirmed dead and 531 are missing in all, state news agency Xinhua reported on Friday. But several families of those missing allege an information blackout in China, worsening their agony. "We are not getting anything from China, whether my sister is safe or alive or dead," said Naresh Goyal, brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, a 51-year-old British national. According to Goyal, UK police visited his sister's family home a few days ago to collect a DNA sample from her daughter to present it to Chinese authorities. China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the accusations, the timeline for victim identification, or DNA collection protocols being used on the Tibetan side. It has said it has been holding briefings for embassies representing 23 countries and on Monday it said its release of information about the floods was "[USN:P8N43C01U TEXT:"transparent and timely"]". Beijing has also said it is ready to work with other countries and agencies to identify the dead. It has sent a group of DNA identification experts to Nepal, which has borne the brunt of the devastation. In Nepal, authorities, including the police, regularly share information on those missing and dead on social media, while search efforts have been accompanied by active DNA testing. China called diplomats from countries with missing citizens reported in Nepal for a briefing last week in Beijing. Diplomats who attended said Beijing shared no details on how it planned to proceed with DNA identification of victims. In addition, China has not offered to provide video from its side of the land port, including facial-recognition images, that could be shared with families or used in identifying the dead, diplomats in contact with China's foreign ministry said. They asked not to be named because the conversations remain private.

MONZA, Italy, Sept 5 : George Russell showed he was the man to beat by setting the fastest time for Mercedes in final practice for the Italian Grand Prix on Saturday, with Formula One title rival and former teammate Lewis Hamilton second for home favourites Ferrari. Russell, who is second overall and level on points with Hamilton in the championship but ahead 2-1 on wins, lapped with a best time of one minute 22.219 seconds at the fastest track on the calendar and one of the most historic. Seven-times world champion Hamilton, who is going for a record sixth Italian Grand Prix win at Monza, was 0.226 slower at the "Temple of Speed", a slipstreaming track where drivers seek an aerodynamic tow from others to go faster. Russell's teammate Kimi Antonelli, the first Italian in 73 years to be leading the championship at the Monza race, was fourth fastest with Red Bull's 2025 winner Max Verstappen third.

Antonelli, 59 points ahead of Russell and Hamilton, is set to start from the back of the grid due to engine penalties - giving his rivals a great chance to cut the gap to the top. Russell was also fastest on Friday after a Ferrari one-two in the opening session. Lando Norris, McLaren's reigning world champion and winner of the last two races, was fifth, 0.406 off the pace, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc sixth. Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was seventh followed by McLaren's Oscar Piastri with Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto completing the top 10. Hamilton and Verstappen almost collided in a late clash, after Hamilton passed the Red Bull at Parabolica before the Ferrari ultimately ran wide, with the stewards taking note. "He caused that," said Verstappen over the radio. "I got blocked by Max," said Hamilton. The top 12 were all within a second of Russell's time.

Sept 5 : Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar has ended his season early to focus on recovery after last weekend's crash during Vuelta a Espana left him with injuries that required surgery, his team UAE Team Emirates-XRG said on Saturday. Slovenian Pogacar, who was leading the Vuelta when the crash forced him to abandon, has also extended his contract with his team until 2032. “This isn’t the way I wanted my season to finish. Right now, the most important thing is to recover properly and give my body the time it needs," the 27-year-old said in a statement. Pogacar, who joined UAE Team Emirates-XRG in 2019, has won six Grand Tour titles, including the Giro d'Italia in 2024.

Sept 5 : Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes has stepped down from his role after a two-year stint, the club said on Saturday, ending a short tenure in which he oversaw the difficult transition after the departure of former manager Juergen Klopp. Hughes, who joined Liverpool from Bournemouth, informed the club's ownership of his desire to seek a new challenge after delivering the 2024-25 league title and Champions League qualification the following season. "Richard joined us at the start of a period of change, embracing that responsibility by leading our football operations department and overseeing recruitment while also providing valuable support to our coaching staff," Fenway Sports Group president Mike Gordon said. "The results we achieved in these areas during this period are testament to this contribution. Nevertheless, we respect Richard's life choices and wish him and his family well in their next venture."

Hughes appointed Arne Slot as Klopp's successor, a decision that paid immediate dividends with a Premier League title triumph in the Dutchman's debut campaign. He also presided over an ambitious recruitment drive, bringing in high-profile signings such as Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike among others as Liverpool invested heavily to compete at the highest level. His tenure was not without controversy, however, with the squad criticised for lacking balance and depth in certain positions despite the significant outlay. Liverpool endured a more difficult 2025-26 season, leading to questions over some of Hughes' expensive recruitment decisions and Slot was sacked when their title defence turned into a scramble for Champions League qualification. Hughes, who has been linked with a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal, expressed gratitude for his time at Anfield. "I would like to reiterate what I said upon my arrival – it has been a source of great pride to have been given the opportunity to serve this incredible and unique institution. That is something I will always be grateful for," he said.

TURMUS AYYA, West Bank, Sept 4 (Reuters) – U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Saturday said there was no plan to force Palestinians to leave Gaza after two Israeli ministers this week floated proposals for the mass removal of Palestinians from the coastal territory.

• “I can tell you categorically there is no plan of the Israelis to displace people out of Gaza against their will,” Huckabee told reporters in Turmus Ayya, a Palestinian town in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

• “There is an open-mindedness (that) if people wish to leave that they should have the right to leave. To incarcerate them in a place they don’t want to be should be an absolute, I think, just disgrace,” Huckabee said.

Show Full Article

• “Nobody is suggesting that there will be forced displacement. The Israelis are not. The Americans are certainly not. I know of no one who supports that.”

• Defence Minister Israel Katz on Wednesday said there was “no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration.”

• Far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir on Thursday outlined a seven-year plan for removing Gaza’s population through what he described as “voluntary emigration.”

• Israel is to hold a general election on October 27.

(Reporting by Ali Sawafta and Alexander CornwellEditing by Tomasz Janowski)

item.title: Americans hit with record-high Labor Day Weekend gasoline prices - Reuters
item.description: Americans hit with record-high Labor Day Weekend gasoline prices Reuters

item.title: Americans hit with record-high Labor Day Weekend gasoline prices
item.description: With the war in the Middle East still raising energy costs, Americans face record-high gasoline prices for Labor Day weekend, just as political campaigns kick off for midterm Congressional elections.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao, Liz Hampton, Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: With the war in the Middle East still raising energy costs, Americans face record-high gasoline prices for Labor Day weekend, just as political campaigns kick off for midterm Congressional elections. The national average gasoline price will probably hit $4.03 on Labor Day, far surpassing the previous record of $3.83 per gallon set in 2012, said GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan. “Gasoline, while not at all-time records, is at its highest level ever recorded this late in the calendar year, meaning Americans could for the first time ever see a national average price of gasoline above $4 per gallon on Labor Day," De Haan wrote in a recent blog post. The national average price of gasoline stood at around $4.13 per gallon on Thursday, up nearly a dollar from last year's average, according to price-tracking service GasBuddy. Analysts say $4 per gallon is a pain point for many consumers. Gasoline prices, among the most visible economic indicators for U.S. consumers, can quickly shape perceptions of the broader economy. With prices hovering above $4 a gallon for much of the year, the issue has become a persistent concern for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. Trump has pledged to lower energy costs. In recent weeks, he [USN:L1N44Q062 TEXT:"stepped up criticism"] of refiners and fuel retailers, accusing them of [USN:L1N4400L8 TEXT:"profiting from elevated pump prices"]. On August 14, Trump said Americans should be willing to pay a "tiny little bit more" for gasoline to ensure Iran could not obtain a nuclear weapon. Labor Day is typically a final summer getaway for many Americans, with many people traveling by car or airplane. Prices at the pump have climbed alongside crude oil prices, which this week jumped back over $90 a barrel after renewed military action between the U.S. and Iran revived concerns about disruptions to global crude supplies. Prices of distillates, which include diesel and heating oil, also increased, driven in part by [USN:L8N44U1CH TEXT:"ongoing attacks"] on Russian refining facilities, which raised concerns about supply disruptions. Retail fuel prices and crude oil typically move in the same direction because crude feedstock is the dominant cost for producing the fuel. DRIVERS CUTTING BACK “It's completely out of control,” Randi O’Brien, 57, said while filling up her truck at a Phillips 66 (PSX.N) near Evergreen, Colorado. Colorado, along with Utah, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, and North Dakota have recorded some of the steepest price gains since the war started. California, Hawaii and Washington currently have the nation's highest average gasoline prices. “I can only afford $15 worth of gas right now,” said O'Brien, who drives roughly 40 minutes round trip each day to work at Home Depot. She partially blames high prices on the rise in crude and fuel exports from the U.S. following the start of the Iran war, which prompted many countries to turn to America for fuel supplies. Refined products exports are up more than 10% compared with last year, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. "We have our own fuel here, yet we're sending it elsewhere,” she said. O'Brien's struggles are being echoed by motorists across the U.S. With the cost of even a routine grocery run climbing and household budgets already stretched, Houston resident Madison Moore, 28, said she was scaling back her Labor Day travel plans. “It used to always be easy to pack up the car, go to Galveston out to the beach and have a cookout or something. People don't want to move like that anymore though," Moore said while filling up at a Shell gas station in Houston. “You would think that our government can do a little bit more for their people when they actually need it." NO WIGGLE ROOM Persistently high gasoline prices are primarily a supply story, said Kuan Dosmuratov, research analyst at consultancy Wood Mackenzie. Concerns about disruptions to energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have lifted both crude prices and refining margins, while attacks on Russian refineries have tightened fuel inventories across the board. Currently, there are few operational and policy levers that can be pulled to boost fuel supplies. U.S. refinery utilization currently stands at 98%, the highest level since 2018. The government has already extended the [USN:L1N4470OC TEXT:"Jones Act"] waiver, allowing easier fuel shipments between U.S. ports. Washington also ended [USN:L1N44H0UL TEXT:"summer-blend gasoline requirements"] early to try to cap prices. U.S. gasoline inventories fell by 1.2 million barrels last week to 205.7 million barrels, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday. This compares with the five-year average for the month of August of 217.6 million barrels. Prices for other refined products have risen sharply as well. U.S. diesel prices this week hit a new record while air travelers over the Labor Day holiday are expected to pay 20% more for tickets than a year earlier, according to AAA. "The public doesn't obsess with diesel but I see a better than even chance that retail numbers will surpass the all-time record of about $5.82 per gallon from June 2022," Tom Kloza, chief energy adviser at Gulf Oil, said. "It presents a worrisome future."

item.content:encoded: Les candidats déclarés à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 en France ont vivement critiqué l'accord passé entre le parti populiste britannique Reform UK et le Rassemblement national (RN) prévoyant le renvoi en France des demandeurs d'asile arrivés par la mer en Angleterre si leurs partis arrivaient au pouvoir. Les réactions ont été nombreuses en France, où le candidat d'Horizons dans la course à l'Elysée, Édouard Philippe, a par exemple fustigé un "revirement" du RN. "Voir Jordan Bardella signer un accord qui prévoit de renvoyer en France les migrants interceptés dans la Manche, celle-là, on ne l’avait pas vu venir", a-t-il ironisé, se demandant si la candidate Marine Le Pen "est sur la même ligne". Samedi en marge de la braderie de Lille, l'ancien Premier ministre et patron de Renaissance Gabriel Attal a dénoncé une illustration de la "soumission" du RN. "On atteint des degrés d'impréparation et de soumission qui sont quasiment jamais vus dans l'histoire du Rassemblement national, récente en tout cas. C'est l'illustration de leur politique étrangère, qui est celle d'une grande soumission à l'égard d'autres puissances", a-t-il dit à la presse. Si cet accord voit le jour, "notre pays deviendrait le garde-barrière des Anglais ? Ne pas voter Le Pen en 2027 devient une question de dignité nationale", a écrit sur X le candidat de La France insoumise, Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Interrogé sur BFMTV, le candidat du parti Place Publique Raphaël Glucksmann a également dénoncé le positionnement de l'extrême droite. "C'est la marque de fabrique du Rassemblement national : la faiblesse quand il s'agit de défendre l'intérêt de la France. Regardez leurs votes au Parlement européen", a-t-il dit. "Nous sommes, nous, les véritables patriotes." CET ACCORD "DÉRANGE", DIT BARDELLA EN ITALIE En visite samedi en Italie pour un forum économique, Jordan Bardella a dit assumer sa décision. Cet accord avec l'extrême droite britannique "dérange sans doute beaucoup de nos adversaires qui sont des 'immigrationnistes' forcenés, qui ont créé les conditions du chaos migratoire et sécuritaire à Calais", a-t-il dit devant la presse. "Donc je me réjouis de cet accord et si demain nous sommes aux responsabilités et que Nigel Farage l'est aussi, nous mettrons tout en oeuvre pour réduire la voilure en matière d'immigration à la fois en France et aussi en Angleterre." "Monsieur Philippe et Monsieur Attal devraient avoir un peu de décence", a aussi déclaré Jordan Bardella sur BFMTV au sujet des deux anciens Premiers ministres d'Emmanuel Macron. "Ils n'ont (...) aucune leçon de gestion de l'immigration à nous donner." Depuis une dizaine d'années, Paris et Londres peinent à endiguer le flux de demandeurs d’asile qui se rendent de France en Grande-Bretagne, souvent à bord de canots pneumatiques. Plus de 16.000 personnes ont été recensées comme étant arrivées au Royaume-Uni à bord de petites embarcations depuis le début de l’année, soit une baisse de plus de 40%. Cependant, le nombre de demandeurs d'asile arrivant à bord de chaque embarcation est en augmentation, les passeurs ayant modifié leurs tactiques. La sécurité aux frontières est l'un des sujets de prédilection de l'extrême droite en Europe. La candidate du RN à l'élection présidentielle française du printemps 2027, Marine Le Pen, fait la course en tête dans les enquête d'opinion. Reform UK, qui a dominé les sondages pendant près de 16 mois consécutifs avant l’été, est désormais au coude à coude avec le Parti travailliste au pouvoir. Les prochaines élections législatives britanniques doivent se tenir au plus tard en 2029. Le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham et le président français Emmanuel Macron ont annoncé jeudi le déploiement de policiers supplémentaires sur les plages de la Manche afin de dissuader les traversées.

item.title: JLR plans 4,000 job cuts over two years amid sales slump, US tariffs
item.description: Jaguar Land Rover plans a voluntary redundancy programme as it targets 1.7 billion euros in savings over two years and seeks to lower its break-even point ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Joe Wertz Jaguar Land Rover Automotive Plc is set to cut 4,000 jobs over the next two years as the UK’s largest carmaker confronts soaring costs, plummeting sales and the effects of US tariffs, The Times reported. Staff were warned late Friday to expect the announcement of the redundancy program which is due to take place on Monday, according to The Times. In a statement to Bloomberg, the company said it is launching a voluntary redundancy program as it targets about 1.7 billion euros ($2.3 billion) in savings over two years. JLR wants to lower its break-even point to 300,000 vehicles and simplify its business in response to global market conditions, according to the statement. It didn’t mention the number of job cuts planned.  The carmaker, which employs about 33,000 people across the UK, is owned by India’s Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The company’s revenue fell nearly 10 per cent in the most recent quarter with pretax profit dropping 69 per cent to 109 million euros. The company’s first electric Range Rover went on sale earlier this month for 154,070 euros, one of the most expensive electric SUVs on the market and nearly £50,000 more than JLR’s combustion-engine equivalent. The high price sets it further apart from cheaper SUVs coming out of China that are taking the UK by storm. The company has also had to contend with higher US tariffs and a slump in demand in China. Last year, the carmaker suffered a cyberattack that brought its global operations to a standstill. The broader tariff environment and competition from Chinese EVs remain significant headwinds for other European carmakers. Volkswagen AG’s supervisory board is backing a restructuring plan that calls for 50,000 additional job cuts.
